scope: Restricted EVM adapter and cooperative execution lifetime checks by the implementation agent; not an independent audit
changes: Strict legacy/EIP-1559 transaction decoding, canonical ERC-20 transfer/approval decoding and exact unsigned-byte comparison after signature recovery
Wallet-owned immutable chain/genesis/token policy; canonical-block state checks, code hashes, simulation, fee/balance/nonce bounds and single-attempt submission
Execution contexts passed through TypeScript and Swift review, approval and execution; closure/expiry/completion invalidate the context; adapters check after asynchronous work before broadcasting
adversarialCases: Changed chain, sender, nonce, destination, amount, calldata, gas or fee in signed bytes
Malformed quantities, hidden authorization fields, unsupported transaction types and unknown contracts
Wrong genesis, stale state, reorg or wrong block height, sender delegation, changed token code and false simulation
Closure or expiry during asynchronous signing; native task cancellation during execution
Concurrent execution of one nonce; uncertain submission with no automatic retry
RPC mismatched response IDs, oversized data, raw error redaction and aborted calls
New native recipient, zero-value and self transfers under EIP-2780/EIP-8037
Malformed signature recovery errors are converted to fixed protocol codes without library data; unlimited allowance sentinel is rejected even in wallet policy
Owning-request cancellation reaches a native adapter running in a detached task; reproduced failure before the request-wide lifetime flag fix

checks.dependencyAudit: zero reported vulnerabilities in root workspace

limits: Execution contexts are cooperative and cannot undo an already dispatched signature or network submission
Restricted EVM methods only; arbitrary contract calls, THORChain routers, permits, messages, blobs and delegated accounts are unsupported
Gas-limit-times-price fee policy requires separate network qualification; no rollup data fee support
RPC answers are not consensus proofs, and token bytecode pins do not attest implementation/storage or future behavior
Attempted nonce memory is not durable; wallet integrations must coordinate nonces and persist privacy-safe submission evidence
Host tests do not establish live network or token qualification; see separate dated network receipts
